topics.label: Course introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and learning outcomes for the lecture series on cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular and tissue mechanisms of cancer development and modeling
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how genetic mutations and disrupted tissue architecture drive cancer development, and how these processes are studied using cell culture models.

topics.label: Histological features and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They detail how invasion through the basement membrane and subsequent metastasis distinguish malignant tumors from benign precursors using histological examples.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and mechanisms of tumor-induced morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the systematic naming of tumors across tissue types and explain the pathophysiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and mortality patterns across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine statistical patterns of tumor occurrence and mortality in humans and compare cancer susceptibility across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They describe clinical cancer symptoms and evaluate the methodologies, histological targets, and limitations of population screening programs.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture by summarizing the learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practical sessions.
